title: Interfacial Magnetotransport in a NiI_2/Graphene Heterostructure
authors: Stasiu Thomas Chyczewski, Xiaotong Xu, Wenjuan Zhu
abstract: We investigate magnetotransport in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer graphene and the insulating helical antiferromagnet NiI$_2$. While NiI$_2$ is highly resistive and thus poorly suited for direct transport measurements, we demonstrate that magnetotransport in an adjacent graphene layer provides an electrical readout of magnetic-state-dependent interfacial behavior. Most notably, first-harmonic longitudinal magnetoresistance under in-plane magnetic fields exhibits large, anisotropic low-field peaks that are absent from a monolayer graphene/h-BN control device and are suppressed above the multiferroic transition temperature of NiI$_2$. Temperature-dependent harmonic measurements provide complementary evidence: the second-harmonic resistance shows the clearest nonlinear contrast relative to the control device, while the third harmonic contains a larger generic nonlinear and thermal background that is nevertheless modified in the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that graphene-based transport measurements offer a sensitive, non-invasive probe of magnetic phase behavior in electrically insulating van der Waals magnets, opening routes toward spintronic devices based on insulating vdW multiferroics.
summary: The study investigates magnetotransport in $	ext{NiI}_2$/Graphene heterostructures to read out the magnetic state of the insulating $	ext{NiI}_2$. By measuring linear and nonlinear electrical responses, the authors show that characteristic anomalies track $	ext{NiI}_2$'s magnetic transitions. This establishes graphene as a sensitive, non-invasive probe for spintronic applications using insulating van der Waals magnets.
main_problem: The study aims to probe magnetic phase behavior within electrically insulating van der Waals magnets ($	ext{NiI}_2$) using electrical transport measurements.
main_result: Magnetotransport features, particularly large anisotropic low-field peaks in the first harmonic and distinct nonlinear signals in the second harmonic, are observed in graphene/$	ext{NiI}_2$ heterostructures, confirming an interfacial coupling to $	ext{NiI}_2$'s magnetic state.
method: The research employs magnetotransport measurements (longitudinal magnetoresistance) and temperature-dependent analysis of nonlinear electrical responses ($	ext{2}\omega$ and $	ext{3}\omega$) on the heterostructure, comparing results against a graphene/h-BN control device.
model_or_system: The physical system is a van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer graphene (the conducting readout layer) interfaced with the insulating helical antiferromagnet $	ext{NiI}_2$. The measurements probe magnetic proximity effects at this interface.
key_observables: First-harmonic longitudinal magnetoresistance ($	ext{MR}$), second-harmonic resistance ($2\omega$), third-harmonic resistance ($3\omega$), and magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Multiferroic transition temperature of $	ext{NiI}_2$ ($	ext{T}_{	ext{N}2} \approx 59 	ext{ K}$), in-plane vs. out-of-plane magnetic fields, and measurement harmonics.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the observed transport anomalies are due to interfacial coupling with $	ext{NiI}_2$'s magnetic state, rather than generic graphene properties or purely thermal effects (though Joule heating remains a concern for higher harmonics).
figures_summary: Figures show basic device diagrams and SQUID M-H curves; subsequent figures detail temperature dependence of linear resistance, first derivative, second harmonic ($2\omega$), and third harmonic ($3\omega$) responses, alongside $	ext{MR}$ sweeps comparing the heterostructure to control graphene.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of presenting the physical system ($	ext{NiI}_2$/Graphene), detailing multiple measurement techniques (linear MR, nonlinear harmonics, temperature dependence), and systematically contrasting the results against a non-magnetic control device to isolate the magnetic contribution.
why_interesting: This work is interesting because it demonstrates an electrical readout mechanism for magnetism in insulating materials using 2D conductors, providing a platform analogous to how quantum systems are probed via coupling to external fields or substrates.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) Basic diagram of the graphene/NiI2 heterostructure. (b) Optical image of a Gr/NiI2/h-BN heterostructure. This sample is made with monolayer graphene (see Fig. S3). Scale bar: 10 µm. (c) Mass-normalized magnetization curves for a field applied in-plane at various temperatures. (d) In-plane susceptibility measurements zoomed in at transition temperatures under zero field cooling (ZFC), negative field cooling (NFC), and positive field cooling (PFC) conditions. Cooling fields were ± 1 T. For measurements across a larger range, see Fig. S2.

Figure 2: (a) Fundamental four-point longitudinal resistance vs. temperature (b) First derivative of data in (a). (c) Second harmonic longitudinal resistance vs. temperature. (d) Third harmonic longitudinal resistance vs. temperature. Note (d) is plotted on a log scale. In each plot, the dashed lines correspond to critical temperatures.

Figure 3: (a) Magnetoresistance sweeps for an in-plane field applied perpendicular (90 de- grees) to the direction of current flow. (b) Magnetoresistance sweeps for an in-plane field applied parallel (0 degrees) to the direction of current flow. Measurements were conducted with a four-terminal geometry and represent the fundamental (first harmonic) response.

Figure 4: (a) Second and (b) third harmonic resistance of MR sweeps shown in Fig. 3a (field perpendicular to current). (c) Second and (d) third harmonic resistance of MR sweeps shown in Fig. 3b (field parallel to current). The dashed lines in each figure highlight peaks that appear across lower temperature measurements.
